P1.record_note: Scope and novelty. Project P1 aims to replace the assumed topological step (FaceCount) in Trees Cannot Cut (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21686446) with machine-checked theorems about finite rasters. Its first result, Gray's 1971 bit-quad formula for the Euler characteristic of an 8-connected binary image (IEEE Transactions on Computers C-20(5):551-561, doi:10.1109/T-C.1971.223289), is a Lean 4 formalization of a known formula, not a new result. We are not aware of an earlier machine-checked proof, but we have not searched exhaustively and claim no novelty. Until the remaining rungs (L2 and L3) are proved, the FaceCount assumption is not discharged.

P2.record_note: Scope and novelty. Project P2 re-proves the formal cores of Viridis OS decision kernels so that anyone can re-check them with the current public Lean 4 toolchain. These are classical, elementary results, not new theorems: the first, Carbon Continuity, is the 2x2 case of the Collatz-Wielandt characterisation of the Perron root of a nonnegative matrix (A. Berman and R. J. Plemmons, Nonnegative Matrices in the Mathematical Sciences, SIAM 1994, doi:10.1137/1.9781611971262). Each result holds only inside its stated model. It says nothing about coefficient values for any site, whether deployed kernel code implements the rule faithfully, or any carbon-credit or treatment outcome.

P3.record_note: Scope and novelty. Project P3 states and proves the formal core of a circular-economy kernel for Viridis OS: loop mass balance, cascaded recovery, a recovery-adjusted work floor and an N-partner symbiosis condition. These are elementary accounting and inequality results about the stated models, not new theorems. The N-partner condition generalises the two-partner Reciprocity Corridor (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21971047), and the work floor extends the Useful and Dissipated Work Ledger (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22736716). We have not searched the literature exhaustively and claim no novelty. Each result holds only inside its stated model. It says nothing about any measured recovery rate, retention, cost, value or material, about whether deployed kernel code implements the rule faithfully, or about any environmental outcome. The work floor is a bound on modelled efficiency; it is not a Landauer bound and does not rely on the Intelligence Bound, which remains a conjecture.

P4.record_note: Scope and novelty. Project P4 re-executes pre-registered tests of Trees Cannot Cut (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21686446) on real wildfire records. Each test was frozen and publicly registered before its outcome data were requested; this record reports the registered analysis, re-run unchanged, and the verifier's confirmation that it reproduces the reported numbers. The studies are observational. They do not show that barriers stop fires, and the pre-specified checks reported in the paper bound each result. The label TESTED certifies that the registered computation gives these numbers from the registered input files. It does not certify the agencies' source data, the choice of model or the interpretation. The input files are derived from public United States sources (FPA FOD, TIGER, NHD, LANDFIRE, gridMET, MTBS).

P5.record_note: Scope and novelty. Project P5 is a correction. It checks with the Lean kernel that an unrestricted axiom in an early Viridis source (January 2026) is false as written, and that an early theorem named no_finite_compensation proves the opposite of its name. The statements proved here are elementary facts about the algebra cap = P*D/C and are not new theorems. They say nothing about whether any agent preserves biodiversity, about any measured quantity, or about the Intelligence Bound as a physical conjecture, which remains a conjecture.
